note: Written for VAAKYA as general financial education. Must be reviewed for accuracy before release (FR-EDU-07). No product recommendations.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: An emergency fund is money kept aside only for surprises: a medical bill, a repair, or a month with no income. It stops a bad month from turning into a loan.

sections.heading: How much
sections.body: A common rule is three months of household expenses if your income is steady, and six months if it changes or comes by season. Start smaller: even one month helps.

sections.heading: Where to keep it
sections.body: Somewhere safe that you can reach within a day or two, such as a savings account or a recurring deposit you can break. Not in shares, and not lent to others.

sections.heading: How to build it
sections.body: Move a fixed amount on payday, or a percentage of each payout if your income varies. Refill it after you use it.

quiz.q: What is an emergency fund for?
options: Unexpected costs or a month without income

quiz.q: Someone whose income changes every month should usually aim for:
A good place for an emergency fund is:
options: A savings account you can reach quickly

sections.heading: Pay yourself first
sections.body: Decide your saving before you spend, and move it as soon as money arrives. What is left is for spending.

sections.heading: Needs, wants, saving
sections.body: Group spending into needs (rent, food, school fees, EMIs), wants (eating out, new phone) and saving. Cut wants first when money is short.

sections.heading: Track a month
sections.body: Write down every expense for one month. Most people find two or three small habits that add up to a large amount.

options: Spend first, save what is left
Move your saving as soon as income arrives
Buy something for yourself on payday

quiz.q: When money is short, which usually gets cut first?
Why track expenses for a month?
options: To find where money actually goes

sections.heading: Never share an OTP or PIN
sections.body: A one-time password (OTP), UPI PIN or card PIN is only for you. Banks, government offices and delivery companies do not ask for them. Anyone who asks is trying to take your money.

sections.heading: Receiving money never needs a PIN
sections.body: On UPI, you enter your PIN only to send money. If someone asks you to enter a PIN or scan a code to receive money, it is a scam.

sections.heading: Urgency is a warning sign
sections.body: Messages saying your account or KYC will be blocked today, or that you won a prize, want you to act before you think. Stop and check through the official app or the number on your card.

sections.heading: If you lose money
sections.body: Call the national cyber crime helpline 1930 quickly and report at cybercrime.gov.in. Call your bank on its official number to block the transaction.

quiz.q: Your bank calls and asks for the OTP you just received. You should:
options: Share it, it is the bank

quiz.q: To receive money on UPI you need to:
options: Do nothing: receiving needs no PIN

quiz.q: A message says your KYC expires today and gives a link. This is:
The national cyber crime helpline number is:

sections.heading: What a SIP is
sections.body: A Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) is a way to put a fixed amount into a mutual fund every month. It is a method of investing, not a product with a fixed return.

sections.heading: Risk and time
sections.body: Equity funds can fall in value, sometimes for years. They suit goals more than five years away. Money you need soon, or your emergency fund, should not be in equity.

sections.heading: Checking a fund
sections.body: Mutual funds are regulated by SEBI. Check that the fund house is SEBI-registered, read the expense ratio, and be wary of anyone promising a fixed or guaranteed return.

options: A product with a guaranteed return
A way of investing a fixed amount regularly

quiz.q: Equity mutual funds are better suited to goals that are:
Someone promises a guaranteed 3% a month from a fund. You should:
options: Be very cautious: funds cannot guarantee returns

sections.heading: Why insure
sections.body: Insurance protects your family from a loss they could not pay for themselves, such as the death of an earning member, a hospital stay, or crop failure.

sections.heading: Term insurance
sections.body: Term life insurance pays a sum to your family if you die during the term. It has no maturity payout, which is why the premium is low for a large cover.

sections.heading: Mixing insurance and investment
sections.body: Products such as ULIPs and endowment plans combine insurance with investment. Compare their cover, charges and lock-in with buying term insurance and investing separately before you decide.

sections.heading: Health insurance
sections.body: A health policy pays hospital bills. Check what is covered, waiting periods and whether your nearby hospitals are in the network.

options: The insured person dies during the term

quiz.q: Before buying a ULIP, a sensible step is to:
options: Compare it with term insurance plus separate investing
Buy it because it has insurance

quiz.q: In a health policy you should check:
options: Only the colour of the card

sections.heading: The real cost of a loan
sections.body: Look at the total you will repay and the effective yearly rate, including processing fees. A small weekly payment can hide a very high yearly rate.

sections.heading: Credit score
sections.body: A credit score summarises how you have repaid loans and cards. Paying EMIs on time, keeping card balances low and not applying for many loans at once help it.

sections.heading: Instant loan apps
sections.body: Some apps lend without naming a registered lender, charge large fees and ask to read your contacts or photos. Borrow only from banks and lenders regulated by RBI, and never give an app access to your contacts.

sections.heading: How much EMI is too much
sections.body: When EMIs take a large share of your monthly income, one bad month can force another loan. Many guides suggest keeping all EMIs well under 40% of income.

quiz.q: To compare loans, the most useful number is:
options: The effective yearly rate including fees

quiz.q: A loan app asks for access to your contacts. This is:

options: Applying for many loans in one week
Using the full card limit every month
